key_insight: The paper proves that the classical 2-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm always stabilizes in linear time, specifically within 5(n−1) rounds, tightening the long-standing upper bound.
engineering_relevance: This gives a sharper worst-case complexity guarantee for a core graph refinement routine used in graph isomorphism, algebraic graph analysis, and learning-based graph pipelines.
method: Analyze the stabilization behavior of the classical 2-WL color refinement process.
Prove a universal upper bound of 5(n−1) iterations for n-vertex graphs.
Extend the argument to k-dimensional WL, yielding improved bounds for all k≥3.
evidence_signal: The result is theoretical and comparison-based: it improves the prior O(n log n) upper bound and matches the known Ω(n) lower bound asymptotically.
watch_item: The bound concerns iteration count in worst-case analysis; practical runtime and memory use can still vary significantly with implementation and graph size.
paper_title: The Classical Weisfeiler-Leman Algorithm Stabilizes in $O(n)$ Rounds
